name: Identify events involving chance
description: Student can identify everyday events and activities that involve chance.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says tossing a coin involves chance but the sun rising does not.
commonError: Student calls events certain to happen 'chance' events.
checkpointTask: Name everyday events. Ask the student which ones involve chance.

name: Describe an outcome as likely or unlikely
description: Student can describe a possible outcome as likely or unlikely.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says it is likely to rain when the sky is full of dark clouds.
commonError: Student labels outcomes by what they want rather than how likely they are.
checkpointTask: Pose situations. Ask the student whether an outcome is likely or unlikely.

name: Identify certain and impossible events
description: Student can identify events that are certain or impossible.
exampleOfSuccess: The student says rolling a 7 on a normal dice is impossible.
commonError: Student confuses unlikely with impossible, or certain with likely.
checkpointTask: Name events. Ask the student which are certain and which are impossible.

name: Order events by likelihood
description: Student can order several everyday events from least to most likely.
exampleOfSuccess: The student orders 'snow today', 'rain today', 'sun comes up' from least to most likely.
commonError: Student orders by preference rather than likelihood.
checkpointTask: Give several events. Ask the student to order them by how likely they are.

name: Explain reasoning about likelihood
description: Student can explain the reasoning behind their judgement of likelihood.
exampleOfSuccess: The student explains a 6 is as likely as a 1 because each face is the same.
commonError: Student gives a judgement with no reason, or a reason unrelated to chance.
checkpointTask: After the student judges likelihood, ask them to explain why.

name: Identify possible outcomes
description: Student can identify the possible outcomes of a simple chance experiment.
exampleOfSuccess: For tossing a coin, the student says the outcomes are heads or tails.
commonError: Student lists outcomes that cannot happen, or misses possible ones.
checkpointTask: Name a chance experiment. Ask the student to list the possible outcomes.

name: Record results in a tally chart
description: Student can record the results of chance trials in a tally chart.
exampleOfSuccess: Rolling a dice, the student tallies each result in the matching row.
commonError: Student records in the wrong row, or loses count of the tallies.
checkpointTask: Have the student run trials and record results in a tally chart.

name: Conduct repeated trials
description: Student can conduct repeated trials of a chance experiment and record each result.
exampleOfSuccess: The student tosses a coin 20 times and records each result.
commonError: Student stops after a few trials, or does not record every result.
checkpointTask: Ask the student to run repeated trials of a chance experiment and record them.

name: Recognise and discuss variation
description: Student can recognise and discuss the variation in results across trials.
exampleOfSuccess: The student notices they got 12 heads one time and 8 the next, and says results vary.
commonError: Student expects exactly equal results, or does not notice the variation.
checkpointTask: After repeated trials, ask the student to compare the results and discuss the variation.
